articles.title: Google's Advice for AI Overview Citations is Ordinary SEO
articles.summary: Google says optimizing for AI Overviews and AI Mode is still traditional SEO, relying on indexed pages with accurate and up-to-date content rather than tactics like rewriting for AI or adding llms.txt files. However, ranking highly in organic search doesn't guarantee AI citations. Ahrefs found only 37.1% of cited pages ranked in Google's organic top 10. SEO teams need to track which pages AI answers actually reference.

articles.title: Non-Branded Traffic Is Declining. Branded Traffic Is Coming Down With It
articles.summary: B2B organic search is becoming more reliant on branded traffic, but that does not mean branded demand is growing. Across 34 B2B websites, non-branded clicks fell 35% year over year, while branded clicks fell 19%, making branded traffic a larger share of a shrinking organic channel. Generic informational content is becoming less reliable as a traffic source because AI search can answer many queries without sending users to websites. B2B marketers should invest more in product pages, comparisons, pricing, customer proof, and other high-intent content while building brand visibility across reviews, communities, and third-party sources. Organic performance also needs broader measurement beyond clicks, including AI visibility, brand recommendations, buyer consideration, and revenue.

articles.title: Editing workflow for 94 SEM landing pages
articles.summary: AI was used to rewrite 94 paid search landing pages while keeping quality under human control. The work started with writing rules and client-approved messaging to guide the drafts. AI then tailored each page to its target search intent and campaign goals. Every draft went through source-based fact-checking and a 10-role review panel before the original and revised versions were compared by hand.

articles.title: The UX Behind a Notification Dot
articles.summary: A subtle notification badge can encourage account creation more effectively than an immediate pop-up because it sparks curiosity without interrupting browsing. The badge works best when it offers a low-commitment reason to click, such as order tracking, saved preferences, or faster checkout based on the visitor's activity. However, sending visitors to a generic login prompt undermines the experience by asking for an account before they understand its value. Test three approaches: no notification, an entrance pop-up, and a persistent badge tied to visitor activity. Measure login starts, account completions, add-to-cart rates, and purchases to see which approach builds customer relationships without hurting conversions.

articles.title: How Brands Are Winning With Boomers
articles.summary: Brands targeting boomers are finding growth by tailoring their creative, media mix, and purchasing experience to an underserved audience rather than trying to appeal to younger consumers. Skechers markets hands free shoes through familiar personalities like Martha Stewart, while Boarderie uses calmer Meta ads focused on sending gifts to distant family members after discovering women 65 and older were its largest buyer group. Laura Geller brings QVC-style live shopping to TikTok Shop through 18 to 20 hours of weekly livestreams and more than 20,000 affiliates. Frøya Organics concentrates its skincare advertising on Facebook and Instagram rather than chasing TikTok trends.

articles.title: 7 steps to building your own website with AI
articles.summary: Use Claude Design and Paper to build a website without coding, then host it on Vercel. Start with your website copy and brand assets, including fonts and visual references. Design the homepage first before creating other pages. Connect existing tools like Funnel Gorgeous for bookings and beehiiv for newsletter sign-ups. Ask Claude to help publish the site, configure your domain, and run an SEO/AEO audit.

articles.title: AI Sentiment Analysis for Brands: How to Track and Improve What AI Says About You
articles.summary: AI sentiment analysis shows how AI assistants describe your brand, the criticisms buyers encounter, and the strengths they associate with competitors. Track both provoked prompts that test known concerns and unprovoked prompts that reveal opinions AI introduces on its own. Compare sentiment across competitors, products, platforms, and topics, then investigate the cited sources to determine whether negative claims reflect outdated information, factual errors, or genuine product weaknesses. Use those findings to update website content, request corrections from publishers, address product problems, and develop marketing assets such as comparison pages, case studies, ads, landing pages, and sales emails.

articles.title: Organic Sephora Sale Hauls Show Whether Beauty Marketing is Working
articles.summary: Repeated creator recommendations can have more impact than a single viral post. AI tools can track which brands and products appear in social videos even when they aren't tagged. Product-level mentions reveal which items drive interest, while sentiment analysis helps distinguish genuine recommendations from negative feedback. Brands can also use these insights to understand differences in shopping preferences across age groups.

articles.title: Top 5 reasons your content is failing in 2026
articles.summary: Most failing B2B content tries to appeal to everyone and never asks for the sale. Teams skip choosing a narrow audience and positioning, so posts end up as generic advice readers can already get from AI tools. They publish without a repurposing system, which leads to stop-and-go posting that most abandon within weeks. They also hide their offer and skip outreach to people who are already engaged, which can lose half of potential deals.
